fundamental.headline: Strong business, but expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 47% over the last year, it keeps 30 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, its debt is easily covered by earnings.

fundamental.take: Great business, but you're paying up for it: fine to own, better to add slowly or wait for a pullback. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 10% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 47% last year; 27%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 104% (3 years ago -14%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $104 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 127%.

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $182M.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 27%/yr over 3 years and 4%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 40% vs a 5-year range of -8–40% (median 17%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $1.2B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($547M buybacks + $649M dividends) = 1.1% of the company's market value. Share count up 2.7% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $65.34, up 18% in 90 days (up 18% in the last 30); 17 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $39.98, up 11% in 90 days (up 11% in the last 30); 18 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By region, latest quarter vs a year earlier: SG 47% of sales, up 90%; US 42% of sales, up 30%; NL 11% of sales, up 122%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.read: Not enough history to compare with a year ago.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 73% from a year ago and speeding up (from 44% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $40 of operating profit, up from $23 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It turned 95% of its reported profit into spare cash: the profits are real money, not just accounting.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 24× last year's profit (higher than 59% of the last 5 years); only 7× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 18% in 90 days (17 raised, 1 cut lately): forecasts are moving up fast.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
